name.text: Relations Q5 - What the vertical line test tells us

questiontext.text:
How does the vertical line test help to decide whether a graph represents a function?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The vertical line test checks whether a graph represents a function. Imagine a vertical line drawn at some value of \(x\). Every point where it meets the graph is an output for that one input. If a vertical line meets the graph at more than one point, then one input has more than one output, which breaks the rule that each input of a function has exactly one output.

So if any vertical line meets the graph more than once, the graph does not represent a function. If every vertical line meets it at most once, it does.

Option A confuses this test with the horizontal line test, which is the one that checks for one-to-one. Option B reverses the conclusion: meeting every vertical line at most once is exactly what a function does. Option D draws a conclusion about many-to-one that a vertical line cannot tell you, since a vertical line looks at one input at a time. The correct answer is C.

questionnote.text: Fixed: vertical line test, key C.

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic.

falsefeedback.text: A vertical line fixes one input value \(x\). Each point where it meets the graph is an output for that input. Ask what it means for a function if one input has two outputs.
